dek: Dune: Part Three, Doomsday, HBO's Harry Potter and the 100th Macy's Parade lead December.

slides.label: Dec 18
slides.text: Dune: Part Three and *Avengers: Doomsday* open the same Friday, Dec. 18. Pick your snacks.

slides.label: Parade
slides.text: The *100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade* kicks it off Thursday, Nov. 26, free on NBC.

slides.label: Streaming
slides.text: Netflix drops a new *Pride and Prejudice* and the *final season of Emily in Paris* this month.

slides.label: HBO Potter
slides.text: HBO's *Harry Potter* series starts at the very beginning on Christmas Day. Eight episodes.

slides.label: For Kids
slides.text: Hexed, *The Angry Birds Movie 3*, Diary of a Wimpy Kid Christmas and Fraggle Rock cover the family slate.

slides.label: Live Events
slides.text: The Game Awards, *Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua* and NFL on Christmas all stream live on Netflix and Disney+.

slides.label: Right Now
slides.text: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping opened to an estimated *$120 million* this weekend.

slides.label: Bottom Line
slides.text: If you do one thing this month, make it *Friday, Dec. 18* at the movies.

December 2026 movies and TV are stacked, and Friday, Dec. 18 might be the biggest movie night of the year.

Dune: Part Three and Avengers: Doomsday open the same weekend, Netflix drops a new Pride and Prejudice and the final season of Emily in Paris, and HBO's Harry Potter series begins on Christmas Day with Dominic McLaughlin as Harry getting his letter to Hogwarts. The 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade kicks the whole month off free on NBC, Nov. 26.

From The Angry Birds Movie 3 for the kids to Werwulf for the adults only, there's a watch for every couch in the house, plus the Game Awards, Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua and NFL on Christmas streaming live.

Which Dec. 18 release are you seeing first, Dune or Avengers?

caption_linkedin:
December 2026 movies and TV releases are a masterclass in scheduling for attention. Dune: Part Three and Avengers: Doomsday chose the same Friday, Dec. 18, betting two tentpoles can split a weekend instead of waiting their turn. HBO picked Christmas Day for its new Harry Potter series, timing a launch to a day when most of the country is already on the couch. Netflix is closing out Emily in Paris and opening a new Pride and Prejudice in the same month, managing an ending and a beginning at once.

For founders and creatives, the lesson is in the calendar as much as the content: know when your audience is already paying attention, and build around that moment instead of fighting it.

Which release date decision stands out to you, the double opening or the holiday drop?
